newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah kill Israeli soldier, hurt five in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah kill Israeli soldier, hurt five in Lebanon.

text.p: Hizbollah guerrillas killed an Israeli soldier and wounded five in south Lebanon on Thursday night in the bloodiest clash in nearly two months, pro-Israeli militia sources said.

Later, Israeli helicopters twice struck Hizbollah bases just outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone. In a separate air raid, a helicopter rocketed a Lebanese army checkpoint north of the zone, Lebanese security sources said.

The fighting on the last active Arab-Israeli warfront came on the eve of Ashoura, the main religious festival in the Moslem Shi'ite calendar marking the climax of a 10-day period mourning the death in battle in 680 AD of the grandson of the Prophet Mohammed.
The fighting occurred as a group of Israeli soldiers got caught in a guerrilla ambush in ad-Dahr Daidaba south of Syrian-controlled Bekaa valley, two kms (one mile) north of the zone.
"Fighting erupted with machineguns and rocket propelled grenades when Israeli soldiers on a military mission got ambushed by an armed group near the Rihan area," a pro-Israeli militia source said.
In Beirut, the Shi'ite Hizbollah said its guerrillas ambushed the group as they attempted to infiltrate outside the zone.
"One soldier has been severely wounded. The wounds of the other four were moderate. They were all taken immediately to Israel," the pro-Israeli militia source added.

The late night attack brought to seven the number of Israeli soldiers killed and to 33 the number of those wounded in guerrilla attacks in south Lebanon this year. Last year, 27 Israeli soldiers were killed in Lebanon.
The pro-Israeli militia sources said that two Hizbollah guerrillas were killed in the clash but a spokesman for the group in Beirut firmly denied the reports.
The latest attack -- the fifth fatal one in 1997 -- was the bloodiest since March 19 when Hizbollah guerrillas killed one Israeli soldier and wounded three others in a similar clash.
Hizbollah leads an Islamic Resistance fighting to oust Israeli troops and their local South Lebanon Army militia allies from the 15-km (nine miles)-wide occupation zone in south Lebanon.
Lebanese security sources gave no immediate word on casualties in the air raids but said a Lebanese army vehicle was burned by an Israeli rocket.
They said an Israeli helicopter fired four rockets in two runs into the hills of Jabal ad-Dahr near the fighting site.

Shortly after midnight, an Israeli helicopter fired one rocket into a Lebanese army checkpoint setting the vehicle ablaze in Zellaya in the western side of the Bekaa Valley, five km (2.5 miles) north of the zone.
The attacks brought to 30 the number of Israeli air raids into Lebanon in 1997.
